A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Wasserstein SGD/SVRG research despite the changed title and layout. All 24 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v3, including Appendices A-D, support comparison; equations, algorithms, and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical derivations and proofs. Its Gaussian example is solved analytically; neither the main text nor appendices report experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical, including its appendices. The retained Gaussian example contains symbolic calculations, without reported simulations or other original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The KL objective, target distribution, Algorithms 1-2, and proposed SGD/SVRG flow equations (18) and (34) are retained. Expanded KL notation and corrections to illustrative equations do not establish a changed proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or experimentally evaluated tasks. The theoretical KL-minimization problem and Gaussian illustration have the same coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. GD, SGD, SVRG, and Langevin methods remain analytical comparisons; the citation changes do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocols appear in either PDF. Revised step-size and approximation conditions concern mathematical guarantees, rather than experimental budgets, metrics, or testing procedures.

E4.justification: The same Gaussian illustration examines SGD convergence and SVRG variance cancellation. No ablation, sensitivity, robustness, or empirical error analysis is added or removed; mathematical corrections are assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or empirical uncertainty estimates. Covariance expressions describe theoretical algorithmic noise.

E6.justification: Neither version contains measured numerical results. The Gaussian example retains the same stated convergence trends, and the principal rate conclusions remain unchanged. Corrections to mathematical expressions are covered under T1.

T1.justification: v3 adds cutoff-function/Fatou arguments in Appendices A/B.1 and revises initial-error propagation in Appendix C. Theorem 2 replaces the broader H1-H3 conditions with Assumption 2 and substitutes previously derived Lipschitz bounds. SGLD noise scaling and the Gaussian covariance sum and square root are corrected. These refine the existing analysis without new principal convergence rates: v3's Theorem 6 restates v1's Theorem 3, and Lemma 3 collects existing bounds.

C1.justification: Both versions claim construction of continuous Wasserstein SGD/SVRG flows through corresponding Euclidean SDEs and Fokker-Planck equations, connections to Langevin sampling, and convergence rates matching Euclidean counterparts.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly qualifies that vanishing Riemannian gradient norm need not imply convergence in other probability distances (Section 4.2, footnote 3). Section 6.2 adds conditions for SVRG's complexity advantage and a heuristic explanation linking its polynomial-growth assumption to choosing the initial density.

D1.justification: Both versions provide mathematical pseudocode and theoretical parameter conditions. Neither adds or removes code/data access information, hardware specifications, runtime measurements, or practical implementation instructions.

R1.justification: v3 adds Liu (2017), Reddi et al. (2016), and Shiryaev (2016), while removing Platen (1999) and Schmidt et al. (2017). New Remark 1 explains the distinction from Santambrogio's minimizing-movement construction. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Prose is extensively revised across the abstract, introduction, related work, preliminaries, and flow constructions. The title and section headings change, terminology is edited throughout, and v1's Section 7 on PL inequalities is integrated into Appendix D.

P2.justification: The two-column main text and references become single-column. Algorithms and long equations are substantially reformatted, appendices are reflowed, and PL-inequality displays move to Appendix D. Neither version contains experimental figures or result tables.

improvement.justification: Corrected SGLD/Gaussian formulas and clearer stationarity qualifications help. However, Theorem 2's new reliance on Assumption 2 creates a mismatch with retained Example 1: Gaussian log densities on R^d are not globally Lipschitz, although v3 says the assumptions hold. v1's broader H1-H3 conditions accommodated this example. These opposing changes to clarity and theoretical consistency leave the net quality effect uncertain.
